Problem Summary:

`transform` have copy and non-copy implemented in the `dest` parameter, sometimes it will return `src` directly, so we can not reuse it.

issue_context.title: wrong result if character_set_results is gbk
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
set names utf8mb4;
drop table if exists t;
create table t(a blob, b char(10));
insert into t values (0x61, '啊');
insert into t values (0x61, '一');
set names gbk;
select * from t;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```sql
mysql> select * from t;
+------------+------+
| a          | b    |
+------------+------+
| 0x61       | ��     |
| 0x61       | һ    |
+------------+------+
2 rows in set (0.01 sec)
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
mysql> select * from t;
+------------+------+
| a          | b    |
+------------+------+
| 0x61       | ��     |
| 0xA1       | һ    |
+------------+------+
2 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

review_comments: Does it mean always copy here?
noop, if we can return `src` directly, the `buffer` is not used in `transform`
I init the buffer in the new commit, PTAL
So if user changed the value of `data`, value of `src` will follow the change. Seems the behavior of `Transform` still inconsistent.
@Defined2014 @xiongjiwei Maybe it is better to add a comment like 'the result is read-only' to `Transform()`.
So the assumption is: on average, there are few parameters in prepared statements?
no, we can not buffer here since there is a `types.NewBytesDatum` use the `decodeInput` result which will take the ownership, it means we must make a new `bytes array`
